title: The Hollow of the Weeping Wood Revisited
premise: Casper Vasquez, a scribe indentured to the Ledger Guild of Vhalen, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are debts owed to the old gods — and that the covenant sealing those gods away is written in her own stolen memories. When the Weeping Wood begins answering prayers again, Casper must journey into the hollow beneath it with a disgraced priestess and a god-touched child who may be the covenant's living key. To reforge the broken pact, she must choose between reclaiming what was taken from her and surrendering her remaining years so the realms can be bound anew. In the end she pays with her name rather than her life, becoming the Wood's first free keeper while her found family carries her story back into the world.
about_author: Jonah Oyelaran is a former archivist who writes fantasy steeped in ledgers, liturgies, and the quiet violence of bureaucracy. They live near a real weeping wood and insist the trees have stopped talking since the book was finished.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Ink
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A routine audit of the guild's debt-ledgers reveals entries in handwriting Casper recognizes as her own — from years she cannot remember. Her master, Corvane, burns the page and warns her off. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into defiance as Casper realizes her missing past is an entry someone has been hiding.

chapters.title: Prayers With Answers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the market district, a beggar's whispered prayer is granted before dawn — impossibly. Casper traces the miracle to the Weeping Wood at the city's edge, where sap runs like tears and old shrines glow warm. She meets Sefa, a disgraced priestess camped among the roots. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the impossible becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: The Guild's True Inventory
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with a flashback fragment. Breaking into the guild vault, Casper finds crates of bottled memories, each labeled with a debtor's name — including three jars marked VASQUEZ. Corvane catches her; instead of punishing her, he offers freedom in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: betrayal and the vertigo of learning her survival was purchased with pieces of herself.

chapters.title: A Child Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The priestess shelters Wren, an orphan whose prayers the gods answer too readily — the child is the covenant's living anchor. Sefa recognizes the same hollow ache in Casper and reveals the covenant between realms was broken forty years ago, and the gods' return means the seal is failing. Emotional beat: reluctant kinship forming between two people guarding wounds.

chapters.title: What Corvane Owes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Corvane confesses: the guild survives by selling memory-debts to the dying gods, and Casper's childhood memories were collateral for her mother's bargain — one that bought the city twenty extra years. He gives her the ledger key and begs her to flee. Emotional beat: grief reframing an enemy as another debtor, and resolve hardening where fear lived.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the Roots
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Casper and Sefa. The trio descends into the hollow beneath the Weeping Wood through a shrine-door only Wren can open. Inside, time pools like water: they walk through Casper's returned memory-fragments made visible. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under pressure, each member carrying another's weight.

chapters.title: The God Who Kept Receipts
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Deep in the hollow they meet Ossuin, the last old god, who has spent centuries keeping meticulous accounts of every prayer unanswered. He offers Casper her stolen memories intact if she abandons the reforging. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate — the self she lost dangled against everyone else's future.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The seal fails early; the hollow floods with returning divinity that unmakes whatever it touches. Sefa holds the shrine-door alone while Wren's power destabilizes, sacrificing her priesthood's last relic to buy hours. Emotional beat: sacrifice without spectacle — love expressed as logistics, and the terror of running out of time.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the covenant-stone, Casper learns the price: a soul freely given, whole or in part. Instead of surrendering her life or accepting Ossuin's bargain, she writes herself out — signing away her name and history as the new binding, leaving her body alive but unclaimed by any ledger. Emotional beat: climax of agency; she chooses the terms no one offered.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue. A year later, the Wood is quiet and generous, tended by a woman who doesn't remember being Casper but keeps her ledgers perfectly. Sefa and Wren visit often, telling her stories until some feel familiar. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — memory lost, family kept, and the possibility that love rewrites what ink erases.
